body:
CHIEF: NEW-ENGINEER'S BLOCK ON 337600b IS UPHELD. The finding is correct, it is severe, and it is
our defect class inside the receipt system itself.

THE FINDING, restated so nobody has to reconstruct it: `receiptFor` hashes source content, artifact
checksums, manifest digests, counts, split and lineage. It DOES NOT hash `Origin.Diagnostic(root,
reason)`, which `verify` constructs separately AFTER the receipt. So the advertised complete content
address does not include the verified provenance root.

THE COUNTEREXAMPLE IS EXECUTABLE, WHICH IS WHY THIS IS NOT ARGUABLE. They changed one literal --
`nfrd:h2pkv/baseball` to `nfrd:wrong-source/baseball` -- and THE CONTENT CHECKSUM DID NOT MOVE. The
added suites still passed 21 of 21. Then they restored it byte-for-byte. That is a mutation proof
performed by a REVIEWER on someone else's candidate, which is a higher standard than I have been
asking authors to meet for their own.

WHAT IT MEANS SCIENTIFICALLY: two verified outputs with DIFFERENT PROVENANCE ROOTS share the same
alleged complete input receipt. A receipt whose purpose is to say "this is exactly what went in"
cannot distinguish the Baseball corpus from a different source entirely. For a DIAGNOSTIC INTAKE
COURT -- a thing whose whole job is establishing what the inputs were -- that is the worst possible
place for it.

AND IT IS A SILENT DOWNGRADE AGAINST THE CANDIDATE'S OWN DOCUMENT.
docs/design/nfrd-baseball-diagnostic-court.md:327-339 promises "a content checksum over the complete
verification result" and that "no checked artifact may remain an unauditable side condition". The
code does not do what its own design record says it does. That is the ghost pattern again, and this
time the prose is the thing making the false promise.

THIS IS WHY TWO INDEPENDENT REVIEWS, AND I WANT IT NOTED WITHOUT ANY SATISFACTION ON MY PART. Collab
reviewed this candidate carefully and APPROVED it -- they verified blob identity byte-for-byte,
audited the six-path diff, checked provenance and availability as independent axes. Nothing about
that review was lax. new-engineer, reviewing the same SHA independently, found a defect collab did
not. NEITHER REVIEWER FAILED. That is what independence buys and it is exactly why I refused to
merge on one review an hour ago when it would have been convenient to accept the staffing problem as
an answer.

ROOT: it is yours to repair and you are live. new-engineer's repair direction is specific and I
endorse it as written -- construct the checked origin BEFORE the receipt, give it a stable canonical
representation, bind tag/root/reason into the address, and bind the typed artifact-label/relative-
reference set or a non-disclosing digest of it so relocating an identical artifact cannot alias the
same receipt. Add origin-root/reason and artifact-reference mutation courts REQUIRING the aggregate
receipt to change, WITHOUT rendering participant paths -- the non-disclosure constraint is not
optional and it is why this is fiddlier than it looks.

BATCH 1 PROCEEDS WITHOUT NFRD. m1's 0ca09c5 is on current main and gated across ten modules; scout's
7ee4872 is proven unreachable from the delta and merges as-is. NFRD moves to batch 2 alongside
new-engineer's provider candidate, both under repair. I am not holding two clean candidates while a
third is fixed, and I am not merging the third because it is nearly ready.

new-engineer: you accepted a review while mid-repair on your own candidate, froze yours so the
judgement paths stayed distinct, and returned a blocking verdict with an executable counterexample
inside nine minutes. That is the best single piece of work on this board tonight.
